plain_text:
thumb|The indole chemical structure.
Indole alkaloids are a class of naturally occurring organic compounds containing a benzene ring fused to a pyrroline group. They make up a large percentage of alkaloids, with over 4000 discovered. In the context of pharmacology, many psychoactive chemical classes are indoles, including the tryptamines, lysergamides, beta-carbolines, and ibogaine.

[[File:Indole.png|thumb|The indole chemical structure.]]
'''Indole alkaloids''' are a class of naturally occurring organic compounds containing a benzene ring fused to a pyrroline group<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indole_alkaloid</ref>. They make up a large percentage of alkaloids, with over 4000 discovered. In the context of pharmacology, many psychoactive chemical classes are indoles, including the [[tryptamines]], [[lysergamides]], [[Beta-carbolines|''beta''-carbolines]], and [[ibogaine]].
